title: Acme Logistics: duplicate charge on invoice 8841
transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling Acme support, this is Maya. Can I get your account ID or the company name?
Customer: It's Acme Logistics, account 4471. I'm calling because we got charged twice for the same invoice.
Agent: I'm sorry about that. Do you have the invoice number?
Customer: It's invoice 8841. We paid it on July 28, and then I saw another charge for $120 on the company card on July 30.
Agent: Let me pull that up. I see invoice 8841 for $120, and yes, there are two settled payments on the card ending 4417. One on the 28th and one on the 30th.
Customer: Right. Our finance team flagged it this morning. We need the duplicate reversed, and honestly this is the second time this year something like this has happened.
Agent: I understand. I'm going to treat the July 30 charge as a duplicate and issue a refund for $120 to the same card. It should post in five to seven business days.
Customer: Can you send me a confirmation? Finance needs something in writing.
Agent: Yes, I'll send an email to the billing contact on the account and include the invoice number and the refund reference. I'm also going to note the duplicate on the account so we can see whether there is a pattern.
Customer: Okay. Do I need to do anything else?
Agent: No. I have submitted the refund. You should get the confirmation within the hour. If it does not arrive by Monday, call us back and reference ticket T-1001.
Customer: T-1001. Got it. And the refund is $120, right?
Agent: Correct. One hundred twenty dollars for the duplicate charge on invoice 8841. I have also added a note that finance should watch the next billing cycle.
Customer: That works. Thank you.
Agent: You are welcome. Sorry again for the trouble. Have a good day.
